messages:
alex: FYI customer ACME reporting repeated 503s to eu-west, then requests auto-route to us-west adding ~800ms. They say tokens were billed even when 503s returned. cc @sara

sara: Thanks — putting on triage. Any alert IDs or logs?

ops-bot: AUTO-SPILLOVER ALERT: id=auto-spill-1999 policy=soft-fallback from=eu-west -> us-west reason=queue_depth>95% duration=12s

marta: Quick dump from eu-west router around the time: `queue_depth=182/192 (95%)`, `spillover_rate=0.78`, fallback_target=us-west. I also see auth failures on fallback path: fallback_router returned 401 for same bearer token. Snippet: ```POST /v1/generate 401 {"error":"invalid_token_scope"}```

alex: Customer says they retried and got 503s then a late 200. They see billing increments for each attempt. Possible double-charge on retries?

eng-ml: This smells like routing policy drift. Soft-fallback should avoid routing requests that rely on region-scoped auth. Check `rbctl get routing policy eu-west` — suspect `allow_auth_mismatch` was toggled on last week.

sara: Confirmed — `routing.policies.eu-west.soft_fallback.allow_auth_mismatch=true` after the 2026-09-14 config push. Rolling it back to `false` in 5m and pinning the customer to eu-west as mitigation. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: CONFIG-ROLLBACK: routing-config for eu-west initiated by sara at 1999993500; status=rolling

marta: Customer repro steps I followed: 1) `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <eu-token>" -H "X-Region: eu-west" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` 2) repeat the same call 3x in ~2s -> result: 1st request 503 fallback to us-west (us-west returned 401 for token), 2nd request 503, 3rd request eventually 200 from us-west after retry. Logs: ```[eu-router] 1999999999 request id=abc queue_depth=176 -> spillover to us-west
[us-router] 1999999999 request id=abc auth=401 token_scope=eu-only
[client] retries=2 backoff=50ms -> final status=200 latency=850ms```

alex: Filed a support ticket and opened billing case — assigning to @billing-team. Also marking this P2 for follow-up / postmortem if config change caused auth exposure.

sara: Rollback finished — `allow_auth_mismatch=false` is live. Auto-spillover still enabled but will block auth-mismatched routing. Monitoring queue_depth and spillover counts for next 30m :eyes:

eng-ml: Follow-up recommendations: 1) add a guard to not consume billing units on fallback retries that receive 401/403 from target region (treat as non-billable retry). 2) add header suggestion for clients: `X-Redwood-Failfast: 1` to opt-out of cross-region retries when they care about token scoping. 3) add metric `fallback_auth_mismatch_count` and alert when >5/min.

alex: Good plan. I'll credit the customer for excess token usage and keep them updated. Closing loop once billing confirms.
